extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers and associate editors for the INFORMS Operations Research journal
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers (and associate editors) who evaluate submissions to the INFORMS journal Operations Research, covering process, confidentiality, editorial decision criteria, ethical standards, timeline, and reviewer best practices. Focuses on what editors expect reviewers to check and how reviews should be written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymous peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations Research uses a double-anonymous peer review process where authors' identities are not disclosed to reviewers, and reviewers' identities are not disclosed to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate manuscripts without knowledge of authorship; submitted reviews and comments must preserve anonymity when shared with authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments to editors are strictly confidential; comments shared with authors will be made anonymous; reviewer names known only to editor-in-chief, area editor, associate editor, and editorial staff; author names confidential to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose manuscript content or identities outside the editorial process; maintain confidentiality of reviewer identity except as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the contribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the explicit editorial decision criteria; reviewers should assess whether the paper addresses an important problem or advances the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of the approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality of the approach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate whether the methods or ideas are novel compared to existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of the writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript is clearly written and organized so that the contribution and methods are understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of the methods and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of the methods and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check correctness of proofs/derivations, soundness of methodology, appropriateness of assumptions, and whether conclusions are supported by results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the journal's editorial statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance to the journal's editorial statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge whether the manuscript fits the scope and aims of Operations Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations Research will never consider an author's race, gender, sexual orientation, religious beliefs, ethnic origin, citizenship, or political philosophy in making editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate manuscripts only on scholarly criteria; do not let any protected characteristic influence judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timeline and 2-cycle goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is to have a 2-cycle review process. The Associate Editor receives the manuscript and within two weeks determines if the paper has the potential to be over the bar for OR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be timely in completing reviews to support the journal's 2-cycle objective; AE triage occurs quickly (within ~2 weeks).

rubrics_metrics.name: AE-requested targeted checks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Associate Editor may ask reviewers specific questions: asking for proofs to be double-checked; comparing methodological novelty to the literature; assessing simulations and numerics for robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to perform focused, technical checks when requested by the AE (e.g., verify proofs, evaluate novelty relative to literature, test sensitivity/robustness of numerical results).

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must not publish manuscripts describing essentially the same research in more than one journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag suspected redundant or duplicate submissions; ensure the manuscript represents a distinct contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authors' previous work when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations to previously published own work required when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect authors to cite and discuss their related prior publications; note missing self-citations when they affect assessment of novelty or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: No concurrent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting the same manuscript to multiple journals concurrently constitutes unethical behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected simultaneous submission; reviewers and editors should enforce single-submission norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques to help authors improve the manuscript; be specific about problems and suggest remedies when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify recommendations with specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify recommendations with specific examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support accept/revise/reject suggestions with concrete evidence from the manuscript (e.g., cite sections, equations, figures) rather than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish major and minor concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish major and minor concerns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate fatal/important issues that affect publicationability from smaller fixes (stylistic, editorial, clarifying points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Be timely
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete reviews within the agreed deadline to support efficient editorial processing and the journal's 2-cycle goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decline when conflict of interest or insufficient expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline if conflict of interest or insufficient expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot provide an impartial, knowledgeable review, decline and, when appropriate, suggest alternative reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal review contents or identities outside the editorial process; ensure comments to authors are anonymized as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternative reviewers when declining
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest alternative reviewers if declining
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you decline, provide names of qualified, impartial colleagues to assist the AE in finding reviewers.
